summary: On-demand chunked SIEM export with ephemeral allowlist, signed manifests, and completed security questionnaire request
description: Issue summary: Customer (NordBank) requested an on-demand SIEM export bundle for a scheduled audit. Requirements include: chunked hourly export files (ndjson.gz), per-chunk signed manifests (Ed25519), RFC3161 timestamp attestations for bundle creation, deterministic per-tenant pseudonymization for user identifiers (HMAC-SHA256 with tenant KEK), field-level encryption for 'session_token' and 'username', and an ephemeral allowlist mechanism (time-limited bearer token) for S3 retrieval. They also supplied a completed security questionnaire and expect a bundled evidence package for SOC2 audit. Impact: customer cannot complete audit evidence submission until we provide the signed, timestamped bundle and mapping doc. Risk: audit deadline 2026-03-18. Environment: prod ingestion -> audit exporter -> s3-us-east-1 (bucket: redwood-nordbank-evidence).
impact: Customer audit blocked; legal/audit team awaiting signed manifests and timestamped evidence. Potential SLA escalation if not delivered by due date.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer requested 'on-demand' export via support portal. 2) Support triggered EXPORT job ID nb-20260314-01 using internal runbook. 3) Export job completed but manifest shows server-local timestamps and missing session_id field for two hourly chunks. 4) Customer attempted to validate signatures and RFC3161 chain and reported validation failures.

investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: manifest generator was using host local timezone instead of UTC leading to RFC3161 validation mismatch against customer's verifier.

Found filter in export pipeline that drops 'session_id' for events older than 7 days if retention flag 'mask_legacy_sessions' is enabled for tenant; NordBank has mask_legacy_sessions=true unexpectedly set in their tenant profile.

Ed25519 signatures are present and verify against our current export key (export-signing-v3), but RFC3161 timestamping used internal system clock and not the CA timestamping service; manifests contain human-readable 'ts' rather than RFC3161 timestamp token.
Ephemeral allowlist token was generated correctly but TTL was set to 1 hour; customer attempted retrieval 2 hours after generation leading to 403 retrieval error in one validation attempt.
No evidence of data leakage; chunks themselves contain pseudonymized username hashes as expected for most rows.

resolution: Planned resolution steps: (1) Generate corrected on-demand bundle for job nb-20260314-01 with UTC-based RFC3161 timestamp tokens and detached token files attached to manifests; (2) Re-run export pipeline for affected hourly chunks with mask_legacy_sessions temporarily disabled for customer to produce backfilled session_id rows; (3) Issue new ephemeral allowlist tokens with 24-hour TTL and provide presigned URLs; (4) Produce evidence package (zip) that includes: ndjson.gz chunks, detached RFC3161 tokens, manifest files (ed25519-signed), HMAC key derivation notes, a mapping document for pseudonymization, and the completed security questionnaire. Deliverables target: 2026-03-15 by EOD. Postmortem: create playbook to avoid local-time manifests and add tenant flag audit on onboarding automation.
